title: RS_Stack_Aggr
description: >
  Aggregates a column of rasters into one raster holding all of their bands,
  ordered by an index column.
kernels:
  - returns: raster
    args:
    - raster
    - name: index
      type: integer
      description: >
        The position of this row's raster in the result. Indexes must be
        distinct and evenly spaced, such as 1, 2, 3 or 0, 10, 20.
---

::: callout-warning
**Experimental.** This function is experimental; its behavior may change without notice.
:::

## Description

An aggregate function: the aggregate form of [RS_Stack](rs_stack.qmd). Sedona
Spark 1.9 calls it `RS_Union_Aggr`.

The result holds every band of the raster with the lowest index, then every band
of the next, and so on, under the georeference of the lowest-index raster. The
index decides the order because an aggregate sees its rows in no particular
order. Indexes must be distinct and evenly spaced: a gap usually means a raster
is missing, which would silently shift every later band, so it is an error.

As with RS_Stack, every raster must be on one grid (the same width, height,
geotransform and CRS), each band keeps its own pixel type, nodata value and
name, and a band's spatial dimensions take the lowest-index raster's names.
Rows with a NULL raster or a NULL index are skipped; a group with no other rows
gives NULL.

No pixel is read: bands are carried over as they are, so stacking rasters that
are still out-of-database does not load them.

## Examples

```sql
SELECT RS_NumBands(RS_Stack_Aggr(rast, i))
FROM (VALUES (RS_Example(), 1), (RS_Example(), 2)) AS t(rast, i);
```
